pivots.stem: What did the professor say the wear on the manuscript parts suggested about how they were used?

pivots.stem: What is the professor's position on the claim that the suites were composed for actual dancing?

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the editors will do about the missing second-violin book?

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the lake cores show about how long the 1870s advance lasted?

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about why the glacier's front has been advancing?

pivots.stem: Why does the professor talk about the Ravnas farm?

pivots.stem: Why does the professor work through a single page of the Ostrand ledgers in class?

pivots.stem: What did the price series drawn from the ledgers show about how the spike spread?

pivots.stem: According to the letters, what did the partners do while prices were at their height?

pivots.stem: How does the professor treat the long-standing explanation that a ring of merchants caused the spike by holding grain back?

pivots.stem: What did the professor say the tag returns showed about where the fish went after the move?

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply about how next year's survey will be run?
settings: It will cover the abandoned bank one final time before dropping it from the rotation
It will work from a chartered trawler rather than the institute's own research vessel

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the jars of preserved samples in the institute's basement?
settings: They show the fish were already spawning there seventy years before monitoring began

pivots.stem: What is the professor's main point about why the spawning grounds moved?

pivots.stem: How does the professor characterize the city council's handling of the demolition?
settings: As more far-sighted than critics allowed, spacing the work over decades so the city carried no debt from it

pivots.stem: According to the tax rolls, who moved onto the cleared ground along the ring first?
settings: Innkeepers, catching travelers who once had to lodge outside the old gates
Weaving shops that wanted the drying yards they could not fit inside the town

pivots.stem: Why does the professor quote from the visiting engineer's report of 1831?
settings: It preserves the last full survey of the fortifications before demolition began

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the rent series shows happened in the old center once the ring opened?
settings: Rents fell across the center as wealthy households moved out toward the new edge

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the Kestler program's observations of the star?
settings: Its images, blurry as they are, show the feature was already present twenty years ago
It found the disk in the first place, as a by-product of a search for something unrelated

pivots.stem: What did the new Aldan Array observations show about the gap in the disk?

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about what is producing the gap?
settings: A companion embedded in the disk is sweeping that zone clear as it goes around the star

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the team intends to do next?

Put the data out ahead of their own paper so that rival groups can work on it too

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply about the weaving of the bands today?

pivots.stem: Why does the professor spend time on the district officer's inventory of 1902?

pivots.stem: What did the team's fieldwork indicate about how a band's worth is judged?

pivots.stem: What is the professor's judgment of Marovic's account of the exchange system?

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the isotope study's conclusion that the animals had traveled from far away?

pivots.stem: What did the bone-by-bone mapping of the main layer reveal?

pivots.stem: What does the professor indicate the project will do next?
